disclaimer: Evidence mapping, not certification. A pass here means a WASP VM reported the technical evidence for that control; it does not mean the site, the client or the MSP is compliant. Auditors assess organisations, not dashboards. Controls marked 'operator' are outside what a VM can show; 'exempt' controls do not apply to a WASP VM, with the reason stated.

reporting.title: VM reported in the last hour

mfa.title: MFA enforced for administrators (hard wall after grace)

admin_ip.title: wp-admin restricted to admin IP ranges

egress_proxy.title: WordPress egress forced through the Squid allowlist

restrict_egress.title: VM's own outbound restricted by port

crowdsec_ok.title: CrowdSec agent authenticated to its LAPI

crowdsec_enforcing.title: Bans enforced (local bouncer active, or upstream at the proxy)

appsec_inline.title: Requests inspected before the application runs (CrowdSec AppSec on and listening)

vuln_fresh.title: Vulnerability scan ran in the last 48h

no_high_vulns.title: No CRITICAL or HIGH known vulnerability installed

vuln_sources.title: At least one vulnerability source enabled

malware_fresh.title: Malware scan ran in the last 48h

tooling_integrity.title: Installed WASP tooling matches the signed manifest

checksums_fresh.title: Core/plugin checksums verified in the last 8 days

checksums_pass.title: No core or wordpress.org plugin file modified

production_profile.title: Production profile (fails closed on unverified images)

backup_local.title: Verified local database backup in the last 36h

backup_offsite.title: Encrypted off-VM backup in the last 36h

central_logs.title: Wazuh agent active for this VM (central log retention)

no_temp_egress.title: No temporary egress open right now

frameworks.name: CIS Controls v8
frameworks.scope: The WASP VM as an enterprise asset: a hardened, single-purpose WordPress server.

controls.title: Detailed enterprise asset inventory
controls.note: The Hive inventories WASP VMs only; the rest of the estate is the operator's.

controls.title: Software inventory
controls.note: Plugins, themes, core, PHP and MariaDB are inventoried by every vulnerability scan.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive data in transit
controls.reason: TLS terminates at the reverse proxy (NPMplus) in front of the VM; the VM serves HTTP to the proxy only. Verify the proxy's certificate and TLS settings there.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive data at rest
controls.note: WASP DEVIATION: off-VM backups are age-encrypted, but the VM's own disk is not (LUKS is deliberately not planned; see TODO.md). Encrypt at the Proxmox storage layer if this control is in scope.

controls.title: Manage default accounts
controls.note: WASP creates a named admin with a random password; there is no default 'admin' user.

controls.title: Administrator privileges on dedicated accounts
controls.reason: Which WordPress users hold administrator is the site owner's decision. wp-forensics.sh admins lists them; the Hive names planted-looking accounts as malware findings.

controls.title: Automated application patch management
controls.note: WASP DEVIATION BY DESIGN: plugins are never updated unattended (an unattended plugin update has itself been a supply-chain compromise vector). Daily detection plus alerting stands in for automation; this control passes when nothing CRITICAL or HIGH is installed.

controls.title: Automated vulnerability scans of internal assets
Automated vulnerability scans of externally-exposed assets
controls.reason: WASP scans the software it runs, from inside. An external scan of the published site (through the proxy) is a separate service.

controls.title: Collect audit logs
controls.note: Apache, CrowdSec and WASP tool logs are collected on the VM.

controls.title: Retain audit logs (90 days)
controls.note: The VM keeps 14 days of web logs. 90 days needs central retention (Wazuh).

controls.title: Automatic anti-malware signature updates
controls.reason: WASP's signatures are vendored YARA rules that change only with a signed WASP release, deliberately: a rule set fetched at scan time is unsigned code run against every file. ClamAV, if installed, updates its own.

controls.title: Test data recovery
controls.reason: Run wasp-offsite-backup.sh restore drills and record them; a VM reporting that its backups exist is not a tested restore.

controls.title: Application layer filtering
controls.note: Without AppSec, CrowdSec bans after reading the logs: filtering after the fact, so this control is partial. With wasp-appsec.sh on, requests are inspected (light ruleset: virtual patches and generic rules, no CRS) before WordPress runs. Squid filters the way out either way.

controls.title: Security awareness and skills training
controls.reason: People and process. Nothing a VM can show.

controls.title: Service provider management
controls.reason: Contracts with hosting, DNS, mail-relay and backup-storage providers.

controls.title: Application software security
controls.reason: WASP does not develop the application. Third-party plugins and themes are covered by 7.x (vulnerability management) and checksum verification.

controls.title: Incident response management
controls.reason: INCIDENT-PLAYBOOK.md is the technical runbook; the programme (roles, contacts, exercises) is the MSP's.

controls.title: Penetration testing
controls.reason: External testing of the published site, by a third party.

frameworks.name: PCI DSS 4.0
frameworks.scope: Supported only where card data never touches the VM: payments by a provider's hosted page or iframe (SAQ A-type scope). A site that takes card numbers in its own form is not a supported WASP configuration and is outside this mapping.

controls.title: Network security controls configured and maintained
System components configured and managed securely
Protect stored account data
controls.reason: By WASP's supported scope, account data is never stored, processed or transmitted by the VM (hosted payment page or iframe).

controls.title: Strong cryptography for transmission over open networks
controls.reason: TLS terminates at the reverse proxy. Card data does not transit the VM in supported scope.

controls.title: Anti-malware mechanisms active and maintained
controls.note: Signatures update with signed WASP releases, not at scan time (see CIS 10.2).

controls.title: Critical patches installed within one month
controls.note: Measured as nothing CRITICAL or HIGH installed now.

controls.title: Automated technical solution protecting public-facing web applications
controls.note: 6.4.2 asks for a solution that detects AND PREVENTS web attacks continually. Log-based CrowdSec bans after the attempt, so without AppSec this is partial. wasp-appsec.sh on adds in-band inspection (light ruleset, not the OWASP CRS); an assessor may still expect a full WAF in front of the site.

controls.title: Payment page scripts managed
controls.reason: With a hosted payment page the scripts live at the payment provider. If the site embeds an iframe, the page hosting it is in scope and its script inventory is the operator's to keep; WASP's CSP header helps but is not an inventory.

controls.title: Access appropriately defined and assigned
controls.reason: WordPress roles are assigned by the site owner.

controls.title: Restrict physical access
controls.reason: A virtual machine. Physical security belongs to the data centre hosting the Proxmox node.

controls.title: Audit log history retained 12 months (3 immediately available)
controls.note: The VM keeps 14 days of web logs. Twelve months needs central retention (Wazuh).

controls.title: External ASV scans
controls.reason: Quarterly scans by a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor, of the published site.

controls.title: Change and tamper detection on payment pages
controls.reason: Applies to the page that hosts or redirects to payment. WASP's file and checksum monitoring covers the server; detecting script changes in the browser needs a client-side monitor.

controls.title: Information security policies and programmes
controls.reason: Organisational.

frameworks.name: HIPAA Security Rule
frameworks.scope: A WordPress site is not a system of record for ePHI and WASP is not designed to store it. This maps the technical safeguards for a site that may receive ePHI incidentally, through a form, and must not keep it. A Business Associate Agreement with the hosting MSP, the mail relay and the backup-storage provider is required before any ePHI reaches the site.

controls.title: Risk analysis
controls.reason: Organisational. The Hive's findings are an input to it.

controls.title: Information system activity review
controls.note: The weekly security report and the Hive are the review record.

controls.title: Disaster recovery plan
controls.reason: The plan is the MSP's. WASP supplies the encrypted off-VM backups it relies on.

controls.title: Testing and revision (contingency plan)
controls.reason: Record restore drills; see CIS 11.5.

controls.title: Business associate contracts
controls.reason: BAAs with the MSP, mail relay and backup-storage provider.

controls.title: Physical safeguards
controls.reason: A virtual machine; facility and workstation safeguards belong to the data centre and the operator's endpoints.

controls.title: Encryption and decryption (addressable)
controls.note: WASP DEVIATION: backups off the VM are encrypted; the VM's disk is not. Document the addressable decision, or encrypt at the storage layer.

controls.title: Transmission security
controls.reason: TLS at the reverse proxy for browsers; the alert mail relay uses STARTTLS or TLS. Confirm the proxy's settings.

controls.title: Policies, procedures and documentation
controls.reason: Organisational.

frameworks.name: SOC 2 (2017 Trust Services Criteria)
frameworks.scope: Security common criteria and Availability, for the WASP VM as a system component of the MSP's service. The control environment (CC1–CC5) is organisational.

controls.title: Control environment, communication, risk assessment, monitoring of controls
controls.reason: Organisational criteria. The Hive is evidence for CC4 monitoring; it is not the control environment.

controls.title: Protection against threats from outside system boundaries
Restricts transmission and movement of information
controls.note: A temporary egress entry (file share, maintenance) lowers this until it closes, within the hour.

controls.title: Prevents or detects unauthorised or malicious software
Detects configuration changes and new vulnerabilities
Evaluates security events
controls.reason: Triage of what the alerts and the Hive show is a person's job.

controls.title: Responds to security incidents
controls.reason: INCIDENT-PLAYBOOK.md and wp-malware-scan.sh remediate are tools for it; the response is the MSP's.

controls.title: Change management
controls.note: Signed releases and installed-file verification; plugin updates are operator-initiated.

controls.title: Recovery plan testing
controls.reason: Record restore drills.

controls.title: Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy categories
controls.reason: Not in scope unless the MSP's SOC 2 report includes them; a brochure WordPress site rarely carries them.

frameworks.name: NIST CSF 2.0
frameworks.scope: Technical outcomes for the WASP VM. GOVERN is organisational throughout.

controls.title: Govern
controls.reason: Organisational context, strategy, roles, policy and supply-chain risk.

controls.title: Data at rest protected
controls.note: WASP DEVIATION: the VM disk is not encrypted (see CIS 3.11).

controls.title: Data in transit protected
controls.reason: TLS at the reverse proxy.

controls.title: Backups created, protected, maintained and tested
controls.note: 'Tested' is a restore drill, recorded by the operator.

controls.title: Log records generated and made available
Networks and environments protected from unauthorised logical access
Computing hardware, software and data monitored
Respond
controls.reason: Incident management is the MSP's; WASP supplies the runbook and remediation tooling.

controls.title: Backup integrity verified before restoration
controls.reason: wp-db-backup.sh verifies each dump when written; verification at restore time is part of the drill.
